about: Eval C — ranking quality of the data layer (DESIGN.md §10.1 C). No LLM involved.
Golden cases encode DOMAIN TRUTH about where scenes are, not whatever the current
scoring happens to return. That is the point: a dataset written from current output
can only detect change, never tell you the ranking is wrong.
Relevance gains: 3 = the defining scene for the genre, 2 = a major scene,
1 = notable. Gains feed NDCG; Recall@k only cares about membership.
Cases with "known_gap" are expected to fail: they document a real shortcoming in
the seed data or the scoring, each with the fix. They are measured and reported but
do not gate CI — so the gap stays visible instead of being quietly dropped, and the
runner shouts if one starts passing.
Ranking is tie-tolerant: positions use competition ranking (equal scores share a
rank), because the tie-break within a score is alphabetical and arbitrary — failing
on it would measure name order, not scene quality.

cases.source: spike S3 metro_ranking: Bay Area 21 bands, Greater LA 14
cases.rationale: Bay Area thrash is the textbook case — Metallica, Exodus, Testament, Death Angel, Ruthie's Inn.

cases.source: spike S3 city_ranking: LA 13, SF 9 (Bay Area splits across cities at this level)
cases.rationale: No must_rank_first: at city level the Bay Area scene is split across SF, Oakland and Richmond, so LA legitimately leads. All three must still make top-3.

cases.source: spike S3 city_ranking: Seattle 23 bands, +53% over #2
cases.rationale: If Seattle is ever not #1 for grunge, the scoring is broken.

cases.source: spike S3 city_ranking: Helsinki 9, Gothenburg 7, Stockholm 6
cases.rationale: The Gothenburg sound defines melodeath, but Finland out-produces it by volume — so the claim is top-3, not first. This is the case the tie-tolerance exists for: Gothenburg and Stockholm currently tie.
Aggregated to country level, Sweden's lead is unambiguous.
Birthplace of the genre; LA is the other undisputed major scene.

cases.known_gap: `locations` has no Seattle metro row, so Seattle's signals roll up to Washington (state) and the metro ranking returns Greater Los Angeles for grunge — wrong by any domain standard.
cases.fix: Seed a 'Greater Seattle' metro and reparent Seattle under it (spike S3 finding #3: metro regions are ours to define; MusicBrainz has no metro concept).
cases.source: spike S3 metro_ranking had Seattle #1 at 23 — the spike treated Seattle as its own metro

cases.known_gap: London ranks first and Berlin is absent from `locations` entirely. The MusicBrainz 'techno' tag pulls in UK big-beat and electronica (Faithless, Groove Armada, The Chemical Brothers), which swamps the actual techno lineage.
cases.fix: Genre disambiguation during ingestion (don't accept a bare 'techno' tag from acts whose primary tags are big beat / trip hop), plus enough coverage to seed Berlin.
cases.source: domain truth: Detroit is the origin of techno (Belleville Three, Underground Resistance); Berlin is its second home

cases.known_gap: Atlanta has no location row at all — the top-500-by-relevance fetch missed it.
cases.fix: Widen the ingestion fetch per genre, or curate the seed for scenes this obviously major.
cases.source: domain truth: Atlanta is a defining hip hop scene (OutKast, Goodie Mob, and the whole trap lineage)
